newsitem.title: UK: BT told its OneNumber deal anti-competitive.
newsitem.headline: BT told its OneNumber deal anti-competitive.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc was told on Thursday to offer its personal numbering servce, called OneNumber, without discrimination against its rivals.
Industry regulator Oftel told BT that the telecoms giant was acting anti-competitively and that it was in "clear breach of its licence".
Oftel said it had ordered BT to stop running the "find me anywhere" personal telephone number service in its current form because it contained a voicemail element which was an enhanced service.
BT was not allowing rivals access to the network services they needed to provide a rival voicemail service, Oftel said.

The telecoms giant has until October 31 to make available the necessary network services to its competitors and in the meantime, is prohibited from signing up any new customers to the voicemail element of OneNumber, Oftel stated.
